title: ​Nursing as an economic engine
description: THERE is a growing recognition in the Philippines that rapid developments in technology, particularly areas affected by artificial intelligence (AI), are putting greater pressure on the country’s labor market. Already, the skills gap has become critical; according to an analysis by the World Economic Forum last year, an estimated 68 percent of the Filipino workforce will need additional training by 2030 to remain viable, far above the 47-percent global average. As a consequence, much of the government’s strategy toward job creation has been to focus on “upskilling” the workforce, and to update training for entry-level workers through platforms such as the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (Tesda).
